subject.title: [Feature]: Audio file support in read tool (multimodal parity with images)

question: Should OpenClaw add native audio attachments to the core read-tool contract, and what raw-media egress, fallback, provider-routing, and session/audit policy should govern that path?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the solution changes local media forwarding to providers and normalized session semantics, which automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Design the native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider transport, explicit egress policy, byte limits, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

options.title: Keep audio transcription-only for now
options.body: Leave raw audio out of read and direct users to the existing STT/media-understanding paths until maintainers are ready to own native audio egress.

options.title: Fold into the broader native-audio tracker
options.body: Treat this read-tool request as a subcase of the broader native audio input design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51667.

recommendation.title: Design the native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider transport, explicit egress policy, byte limits, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the newest current-main read/session contract history and is the best available routing candidate for the product/security boundary decision.
